subject: science
passage: In 1967 Jocelyn Bell, then a graduate student at the University of Cambridge, noticed an odd signal in the charts produced by a radio telescope she had helped build: a series of pulses arriving every 1.33 seconds with clocklike regularity. The source turned out to be a pulsar, a rapidly spinning neutron star that sweeps beams of radio waves across space like a lighthouse. In the decades since that discovery, astronomers ______ thousands of additional pulsars, some of which rotate hundreds of times per second.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The phrase "In the decades since that discovery" describes a period that began in the past and continues up to the present. An action spread over such a period takes the present perfect: "have found." The present-tense "rotate" later in the sentence confirms that the time frame reaches the present.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The simple past "found" treats the discoveries as finished at a past time, but "since that discovery" describes a period lasting up to now.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The past perfect "had found" needs a later past moment to look back from; here the period runs to the present, not to a point in the past.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The simple present "find" describes habitual or current actions and can't be paired with "since" to describe a stretch of time leading up to now.
explanation.D: Correct. The present perfect "have found" fits a period that began in 1967 and continues to the present.
